topic: A person learns their childhood best friend doesn't remember them
text: Walking down the familiar path where we once chased each other, I spot them—the friend I thought was a cornerstone of my childhood. They look up, the face so etched in my memories, yet the spark of recognition doesn’t flicker in their eyes. I step closer, uneasy laughter bubbling up, trying to mask the twist in my gut. "Hey, remember me? We built forts, chased fireflies, and talked about everything under the sun." Their expression remains blank, a polite smile that doesn’t reach their eyes. The silence stretches, but instead of despair, I find myself weaving a tapestry of new stories, eager to mend the gap, to reignite the connection. Maybe it’s not about the past; maybe it can be about the future.
